assessmentPlatform: Variable (Codility / HackerRank / Teams Live Coding depending on org and campus vs experienced track)

stages.name: Online Technical Assessment
stages.format: Automated coding assessment (typically 2-3 algorithmic problems in 70-90 minutes)
rubricTraps: Hidden edge cases (integer overflow, empty inputs, null pointer handling)
Time complexity penalties on sub-optimal O(N^2) approaches
Failure to compile or handle custom test cases cleanly

stages.name: Technical Problem Solving & Data Structures
stages.format: Interactive live coding interview with an engineer (45-60 minutes on whiteboard/virtual editor)
rubricTraps: Jumping straight into coding without clarifying requirements and constraints
Failing to explain thought process and trade-offs before typing
Weak dry-running and missing edge case validation
Writing monolithic code without modular helper functions

stages.name: Collaborative Engineering & Growth Mindset
stages.format: System & architecture discussion combined with competency-based behavioral evaluation (45-60 minutes)
rubricTraps: Fixed mindset ('I already know everything' instead of 'learn-it-all')
Inability to discuss lessons learned from past technical failures
Lack of customer empathy or ignoring non-functional requirements (scalability, availability, privacy)
Blaming others instead of demonstrating accountability and constructive conflict resolution

behavioralFramework.name: Microsoft Competencies & Growth Mindset
sampleQuestions: Describe a time when you received tough critical feedback and how you adapted your approach.
Tell me about a complex project where you collaborated across team or organization boundaries to deliver impact.
How do you approach mastering an unfamiliar technology stack under tight deadline pressure?
Walk me through an engineering trade-off where you had to balance feature delivery speed against architectural debt.
